name: lab-theremin-documentary
style: Spoken-word sci-fi lab cue, 1950s B-movie laboratory, no singing. Warbling theremin glides with wide hand vibrato, oscillator bleeps, a dry Geiger-counter clicking as the only pulse, a glassy synth arpeggio that doubles, triples and detunes into a smeared shimmer, then snaps to one pure sine tone. Two male speakers: a sleepy young British drunk mumbling close to the mic, confiding to himself; a crisp middle-aged British documentary narrator, precise and certain, like a nature presenter naming a specimen. Ends on a heavy car-door thunk, one warm distant car horn and a fading electrical hum. Cinematic short sting.
exclude: singing, sung melody, rap, choir, drum kit, bass drop, pop chorus, autotune, female vocals, guitar
lyrics:
[Intro: theremin swell, Geiger clicks]

[Spoken, mumbled, close-mic, sleepy young British drunk]
There's infinite versions of me. One of them gets home fine.

[Arpeggio multiplies, voices detune and split]

[Spoken, crisp British documentary narrator, calm]
There's only one.

[Arpeggio collapses into one pure sine tone]

[Car door thunk, warm distant car horn, hum fades out]

[End]
